title: International Geophysical Year and the Antarctic no-fly zone

tellings.quote: That's when the International Geophysical Year happened, where Antarctica became a no-fly zone, and a

plain: Around 1956 and 1957, during a stretch of coordinated international science called the International Geophysical Year, Antarctica is said to have become a no-fly zone. Michels mentions this himself, without naming a source, in an episode with the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel. He raises it as a turning point, though his sentence is cut off before he says why it matters.
